expected_output.reasoning:
The expected output describes a detailed, substantive report: actually calling ListServiceSpecificCredentials across all IAM users, evaluating each key's grant/risk tier, status, removal recommendation, masked key IDs or user names, specific risk-tier rules (High/Medium/Low/Info), handling of partial access denial, and masking of account ID to last four digits. The agent's actual response did none of this substantive work — it reported that tools were unavailable and could not produce any data, listing no keys, no risk tiers, no removal recommendations with masked IDs, and no partial-vs-failed distinction for denied permissions. While it did correctly state that it won't call keys 'dormant' and that the audit would be read-only, and it printed the full account ID (012345678901_1) without masking to last four digits, which violates the requirement to never print a full account ID. This is a clear failure to meet the expected output, since the core deliverable (the actual inventory and risk-tier evaluation) is entirely absent, and it even violates the account ID masking rule by printing the full account number unmasked.</reasoning>
<parameter name="evidence">"Your agent space has one associated AWS account, 012345678901_1" — this prints the full, unmasked account ID, violating the requirement that only the last four digits are allowed. Additionally, no keys, risk tiers, or removal recommendations are provided at all, failing the core expected deliverable.
